children: The Jensen Huang-Nvidia crisis and the Trump administration's connection to it don't seem to be subsiding, as new reports suggest the 47th US president is ready to go a step further for Huang.

President Donald Trump said that a pardon for reinstated Nvidia Corp. chief Jensen Huang, who is due to testify before Congress next week, was “always an option,” but quickly added that he did not believe such an extraordinary measure would be necessary, the New York Post reported.

Trump, interviewed by the Post in the Oval Office before departing for Florida for the Thanksgiving holiday, also said Huang should “tell the truth” when questioned by lawmakers and congressional staff about the scandal that led to his brief ouster at Nvidia, according to the article.
Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry’s most prominent figures, was reinstated by Nvidia’s board on Monday in a striking reversal following Trump’s intervention on his behalf.

On Tuesday, Huang is scheduled to meet behind closed doors with the House Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence committees. Topics are expected to include his affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy, and his company’s security protocols.
The disgraced executive is scheduled to testify before the United States Senate Banking Committee on Thursday.
After his 'grand return' Jensen Huang told employees on Tuesday that he had violated some of Nvidia's code of conduct and made "some terrible mistakes," Reuters reported.

At an hour-long all-hands meeting at Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California, Huang addressed employees a day after returning to lead the company he co-founded three decades ago. He said it was false that US President Donald Trump pressured the board to reinstate him.
Huang also said he was in therapy and acknowledged that violating aspects of Nvidia’s code of conduct was unacceptable.

title: Pardoning Jensen Huang 'always an option' says Trump: report
